verses.lat: Aspérges me hyssópo, et mundábor: lavábis me, et super nivem dealbabor.
verses.eng: Thou shalt sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed: Thou shalt wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow.

verses.lat: Audítui meo dabis gáudium et lætítiam: et exsultábunt ossa humiliáta.
verses.eng: To my hearing Thou shalt give joy and gladness: and the bones that have been humbled shall rejoice.

verses.lat: Avérte fáciem tuam a peccátis meis: et omnes iniquitátes meas dele.
verses.eng: Turn away Thy face from my sins: and blot out all my iniquities.

verses.lat: Cor mundum crea in me, Deus: et spíritum rectum ínova in viscéribus meis.
verses.eng: Create a clean heart in me, O God: and renew a right spirit within my bowels.

verses.lat: Ne projícias me a fácie tua: et Spíritum Sanctum tuum ne áuferas a me.
verses.eng: Cast me not away from Thy face: and take not Thy Holy Spirit from me.

verses.lat: Redde mihi lætítiam salutáris tui: et spíritu principáli confírma me.
verses.eng: Restore unto me the joy of Thy salvation: and strengthen me with a perfect spirit.

verses.lat: Docébo iníquos vias tuas: et ímpii ad te converténtur.
verses.eng: I will teach the unjust Thy ways: and the wicked shall be converted to Thee.

verses.lat: Líbera me de sangúinibus, Deus, Deus salútis meæ: et exsultábit lingua mea justítiam tuam.
verses.eng: Deliver me from blood, O God, Thou God of my salvation: and my tongue shall extol Thy justice.

verses.lat: Dómine, lábia mea apéries: et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
verses.eng: O Lord, Thou wilt open my lips: and my mouth shall declare Thy praise.

verses.lat: Quóniam si voluísses sacrifícium, dedíssem útique: holocáustis non delectáberis.
verses.eng: For if Thou hadst desired sacrifice, I would indeed have given it: with burnt offerings Thou wilt not be delighted.

verses.lat: Sacrifícium Deo spíritus contribúlátus: cor contrítum et humiliátum, Deus, non despícies.
verses.eng: A sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit: a contrite and humbled heart, O God, Thou wilt not despise.

verses.lat: Benígne fac, Dómine, in bona voluntáte tua Sion: ut ædificéntur muri Jerúsalem.
verses.eng: Deal favourably, O Lord, in Thy good will with Sion: that the walls of Jerusalem may be built up.

verses.lat: Tunc acceptábis sacrifícium justítiæ, oblatiónes et holocáusta: tunc impónent super altáre tuum vítulos.
verses.eng: Then shalt Thou accept the sacrifice of justice, oblations, and whole burnt offerings: then shall they lay calves upon Thy altar.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Júdica me, Deus, et discérne causam meam de gente non sancta: ab hómine iníquo et dolóso érue me.
verses.eng: Judge me, O God, and distinguish my cause from the nation that is not holy: deliver me from the unjust and deceitful man.

verses.lat: Quia tu es, Deus, fortítudo mea: quare me repulísti? Et quare tristis incédo, dum affígit me inímicus?
verses.eng: For Thou art God, my strength: why hast Thou cast me off? And why do I go sorrowful whilst the enemy afflicteth me?

verses.lat: Emítte lucem tuam et veritátem tuam: ipsa me deduxérunt et adduxérunt in montem sanctum tuum, et in tabernácula tua.
verses.eng: Send forth Thy light and Thy truth: they have conducted me and brought me unto Thy holy hill, and into Thy tabernacles.

verses.lat: Et introíbo ad altáre Dei: ad Deum qui lætíficat juventútem meam.
verses.eng: And I will go in to the altar of God: to God who giveth joy to my youth.

verses.lat: Confitebor tibi in cíthara, Deus, Deus meus: quare tristis es, ánima mea? Et quare contúrbas me?
verses.eng: To Thee, O God, my God, I will give praise upon the harp: why art thou sad, O my soul? And why dost thou disquiet me?

verses.lat: Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
verses.eng: Hope in God, for I will still give praise to Him: the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Ego dixi: In dimídio diérum meórum vadam ad portas ínferi.
verses.eng: I said: In the midst of my days I shall go to the gates of hell.

verses.lat: Quæsívi resíduum annórum meórum.
verses.eng: I sought for the residue of my years.

verses.lat: Dixi: Non vidébo Dóminum Deum in terra vivéntium.
verses.eng: I said: I shall not see the Lord God in the land of the living.

verses.lat: Non aspíciam hóminem ultra, et habitátórem quiétis.
verses.eng: I shall behold man no more, nor the dweller in rest.

verses.lat: Generátio mea abláta est, et convólúta est a me, quasi tabernáculum pastórum.
verses.eng: My generation is at an end, and it is rolled away from me, as a shepherd’s tent.

verses.lat: Præcísa est velut a texénte vita mea: dum adhuc ordírer, succídit me: de mane usque ad vésperam fínies me.
verses.eng: My life is cut off as by a weaver: whilst I was yet but beginning, He cut me off: from morning even to night Thou wilt make an end of me.

verses.lat: Sperábam usque ad mane; quasi leo, sic contrívit ómnia ossa mea.
verses.eng: I hoped till morning; as a lion, so hath He broken all my bones.

verses.lat: De mane usque ad vésperam fínies me: sicut pullus hirúndinis, sic clamábo; meditábor ut colúmba.
verses.eng: From morning even to night Thou wilt make an end of me: I will cry like a young swallow; I will meditate like a dove.

verses.lat: Attenuáti sunt óculi mei, suspiciéntes in excélsum.
verses.eng: My eyes are weakened, looking upward.

verses.lat: Dómine, vim pátior, respónde pro me. Quid dicam, aut quid respondébit mihi, cum ipse fécerit?
verses.eng: Lord, I suffer violence, answer Thou for me. What shall I say, or what shall He answer me, whereas He Himself hath done it?

verses.lat: Recogitábo tibi omnes annos meos in amaritúdine ánimæ meæ.
verses.eng: I will recount to Thee all my years, in the bitterness of my soul.

verses.lat: Dómine, si sic vívitur, et in tálibus vita spíritus mei, corrípies me et vivificábis me.
verses.eng: O Lord, if man’s life be such, and the life of my spirit be in such things as these, Thou shalt correct me, and make me to live.

verses.lat: Ecce in pace amaritúdo mea amarissima: tu autem eruísti ánimam meam, ut non períret: projecisti post tergum tuum ómnia peccáta mea.
verses.eng: Behold, in peace is my bitterness most bitter: but Thou hast delivered my soul, that it should not perish: Thou hast cast all my sins behind Thy back.

verses.lat: Quia non inférnus confitébitur tibi, neque mors laudábit te: non exspectábunt qui descéndunt in lacum veritátem tuam.
verses.eng: For hell shall not confess to Thee, neither shall death praise Thee: nor shall they that go down into the pit look for Thy truth.

verses.lat: Vivens, vivens, ipse confitébitur tibi, sicut et ego hódie: pater fíliis notam fáciet veritátem tuam.
verses.eng: The living, the living, he shall give praise to Thee, as I do this day: the father shall make Thy truth known to the children.

verses.lat: Dómine, salvum me fac, et psalmos nostros cantábimus cunctis diébus vitæ nostræ in domo Dómini.
verses.eng: O Lord, save me, and we will sing our psalms all the days of our life in the house of the Lord.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Ad te levávi óculos meos, qui hábitas in cælis.
verses.eng: To Thee have I lifted up my eyes, who dwellest in heaven.

verses.lat: Ecce sicut óculi servórum in mánibus dominórum suórum,
verses.eng: Behold, as the eyes of servants are on the hands of their masters,

verses.lat: Sicut óculi ancíllæ in mánibus dóminæ suæ: ita óculi nostri ad Dóminum Deum nostrum, donec misereátur nostri.
verses.eng: As the eyes of the handmaid are on the hands of her mistress: so are our eyes unto the Lord our God, until He have mercy on us.

verses.lat: Miserére nostri, Dómine, miserére nostri: quia multum repléti sumus despectióne.
verses.eng: Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us: for we are greatly filled with contempt.

verses.lat: Quia multum repléta est ánima nostra: oppóbrium abundántibus, et despéctio supérbis.
verses.eng: For our soul is greatly filled: we are a reproach to the rich, and contempt to the proud.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Nisi quia Dóminus erat in nobis, dicat nunc Israël:
verses.eng: If it had not been that the Lord was with us, let Israel now say:

verses.lat: Nisi quia Dóminus erat in nobis, cum exsúrgerent hómines in nos:
verses.eng: If it had not been that the Lord was with us, when men rose up against us:

verses.lat: Forte vivos deglutíssent nos: cum irascéretur furor eórum in nos.
verses.eng: Perhaps they had swallowed us up alive: when their fury was enkindled against us.

verses.lat: Forsítan aqua absorbuísset nos.
verses.eng: Perhaps the waters had swallowed us up.

verses.lat: Torréntem pertránsivit ánima nostra: forsítan pertransísset ánima nostra aquam intolérábilem.
verses.eng: Our soul hath passed through a torrent: perhaps our soul had passed through a water insupportable.

verses.lat: Benedíctus Dóminus, qui non dedit nos in captiónem déntibus eórum.
verses.eng: Blessed be the Lord, who hath not given us to be a prey to their teeth.

verses.lat: Ánima nostra sicut passer erépta est de láqueo venántium:
verses.eng: Our soul hath been delivered as a sparrow out of the snare of the fowlers:

verses.lat: Láqueus contrítus est, et nos liberáti sumus.
verses.eng: The snare is broken, and we are delivered.

verses.lat: Adjutórium nostrum in nómine Dómini, qui fecit cælum et terram.
verses.eng: Our help is in the name of the Lord, who made heaven and earth.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Qui confídunt in Dómino, sicut mons Sion: non commovébitur in ætérnum, qui hábitat in Jerúsalem.
verses.eng: They that trust in the Lord shall be as mount Sion: he shall not be moved for ever that dwelleth in Jerusalem.

verses.lat: Montes in circúitu ejus: et Dóminus in circúitu pópuli sui, ex hoc nunc et usque in sæculum.
verses.eng: Mountains are round about it: so the Lord is round about His people, from henceforth now and for ever.

verses.lat: Quia non relínquet Dóminus virgam peccatórum super sortem justórum: ut non exténdant justi ad iniquitátem manus suas.
verses.eng: For the Lord will not leave the rod of sinners upon the lot of the just: that the just may not stretch forth their hands to iniquity.

verses.lat: Bénefac, Dómine, bonis, et rectis corde.
verses.eng: Do good, O Lord, to those that are good, and to the upright of heart.

verses.lat: Declinántes autem in obligatiónes addúcet Dóminus cum operántibus iniquitátem: pax super Israël.
verses.eng: But such as turn aside into bonds, the Lord shall lead out with the workers of iniquity: peace upon Israel.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: In converténdo Dóminus captivitátem Sion, facti sumus sicut consoláti.
verses.eng: When the Lord brought back the captivity of Sion, we became like men comforted.

verses.lat: Tunc replétum est gáudio os nostrum: et lingua nostra exsultatióne.
verses.eng: Then was our mouth filled with gladness: and our tongue with joy.

verses.lat: Tunc dicent inter gentes: Magnificávit Dóminus fácere cum eis.
verses.eng: Then shall they say among the Gentiles: The Lord hath done great things for them.

verses.lat: Magnificávit Dóminus fácere nobiscum: facti sumus lætántes.
verses.eng: The Lord hath done great things for us: we are become joyful.

verses.lat: Convérte, Dómine, captivitátem nostram, sicut torrens in Austro.
verses.eng: Turn again our captivity, O Lord, as a stream in the south.

verses.lat: Qui séminant in lácrimis, in exsultatióne metent.
verses.eng: They that sow in tears shall reap in joy.

verses.lat: Eúntes ibant et flebant, mitténtes sémina sua.
verses.eng: Going, they went and wept, casting their seeds.

verses.lat: Veniéntes autem vénient cum exsultatióne, portántes manípulos suos.
verses.eng: But coming, they shall come with joyfulness, carrying their sheaves.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
